summary: Figure F12_loss illustrates the stacked mean loss components for different configurations in the Horizon project. The loss is composed of three parts: G, aC, and hF, with an upper bound denoted as cp_upper. The data shows that the loss components vary depending on the configuration parameters, such as the number of models (m) and the strictness of the settings.
observations: The mean loss for G is consistently zero, indicating no contribution from this component in the loss calculation.
The aC component has a mean of 0.01316, with a range from 0.00000 to 0.04250, showing variability based on the configuration.
The hF component has a higher mean of 0.26321, with a larger range from 0.12750 to 0.42500, indicating it is a more significant contributor to the loss.
The cp_upper component has the highest mean of 0.32270, with a range from 0.16646 to 0.52141, suggesting it is the dominant factor in the loss calculation.
caveats: The data is in theory-mode, meaning the results are based on mathematical formulations and not experimental results.
The sample size is small (28 rows), which may limit the generalizability of the observations.
